report.incident_title: Orders stuck in "Processing", confirmation emails not sent
report.summary:
Confirmed: the incident is partition-scoped, not fleet-wide. Starting at 2026-08-21T13:17:52Z, orders-worker-7 began crash-looping, and at 13:52:15Z orders-worker-2 did the same; those exact pods map statically to Kafka partitions 7 and 2, which are also the only partitions with sustained consumer lag growth. Because orders-worker is the consumer that finalizes orders after they are created and depends on downstream notification, orders assigned to those partitions remained stuck in Processing and did not send confirmation emails. 

Most likely, but not directly proven, a subset of OrderPlaced payloads introduced after checkout-svc v4.1.0 was deployed at 13:05 caused orders-worker to crash on affected messages; the specific suspected mechanism is a schema/deserialization problem related to the new premium gift wrap field. That mechanism remains inferential because crash logs, error traces, and message payload inspection were unavailable during the investigation.

hypotheses.statement: Checkout-svc v4.1.0 (deployed 13:05) adds a “premium gift wrap” field that, when present in an OrderPlaced event, makes orders-worker panic on deserialisation. Because the consumer set uses static assignment (orders-worker-N → partition N), the first bad message on partition 7 put pod orders-worker-7 into a crash-loop starting 13:17; a later bad message on partition 2 took down pod orders-worker-2 at 13:52. While those pods repeatedly restart, their partitions stop being consumed, backlog grows, and orders in those partitions remain in “Processing” with no confirmation email.

facts.text: Change history for 2026-08-21T11:20:00Z..14:30:00Z returned a deploy at 2026-08-21T13:05:00Z for checkout-svc: 'checkout-svc v4.0.3 -> v4.1.0: premium gift wrap option'. This is the only application deploy shown before symptom onset in the broad change query.

Infrastructure events for 2026-08-21T11:20:00Z..14:30:00Z include a Kubernetes BackOff on pod/orders-worker-7 at 2026-08-21T13:17:52Z with message 'Back-off restarting failed container orders-worker (exit code 1)'. This event occurs just before the estimated 13:20 onset.

Infrastructure events for 2026-08-21T11:20:00Z..14:30:00Z include a second Kubernetes BackOff on pod/orders-worker-2 at 2026-08-21T13:52:15Z with message 'Back-off restarting failed container orders-worker (exit code 1)'.

Kafka consumer lag is strongly partition-skewed on topic order-events. Partition 7 lags continuously from 14 messages at 13:20 to 730 by 14:25, and partition 2 stays at 0 until 13:55 then grows to 322 by 14:25, while the reported max of other partitions stays near 0-2. This indicates the issue is limited to specific partitions rather than the whole consumer group.

Orders-worker pod restarts are isolated to the pods that match the lagging partitions under the static assignment scheme. orders-worker-7 is already restarting at 13:20 and rises from 3 restarts to 17 by 14:25; orders-worker-2 begins restarting around 13:55 and rises from 0 to 10 by 14:25. No other orders-worker pod metrics were returned. The restart timing aligns with the affected kafka partitions 7 and 2.

orders-worker metrics since 13:20 show repeated container restarts on pod orders-worker-7 throughout the incident window (counter rising from 3 at 13:20 to 17 at 14:25) and on pod orders-worker-2 starting at 13:55 (0 to 10 by 14:25), while no aggregate request/latency/error metrics were returned. The restarts are partial rather than fleet-wide, consistent with a subset-only processing problem.

orders-worker metrics returned only container_restarts_total by pod. Pod orders-worker-7 increased from 3 at 2026-08-21T13:20:00Z to 17 at 2026-08-21T14:25:00Z, and pod orders-worker-2 increased from 0 at 2026-08-21T13:20:00Z to 10 at 2026-08-21T14:25:00Z; returned data ends at 14:25 though the requested window extended to 14:30.

Topology shows orders-worker consumes from kafka and depends on notification-svc and orders-db. The deployment note says it uses static assignment where pod orders-worker-N consumes partition N, so a problem in a specific worker pod can isolate to its assigned partition rather than causing a full outage.

Topology shows orders-worker consumes from kafka and depends directly on orders-db and notification-svc; it runs as a 12-pod StatefulSet with static partition assignment (orders-worker-N consumes partition N) and no dead-letter queue, so failures can affect only a subset of orders tied to specific pods/partitions or downstream calls on the processing path.

corrective_actions.action: Temporarily roll back checkout-svc v4.1.0 or suppress emission of the newly added premium-gift-wrap field while the affected partitions are recovered.
corrective_actions.rationale: The checkout-svc 13:05 deploy is the only application change before symptom onset, and the leading hypothesis is that a newly introduced payload variant is triggering the partition-specific worker crashes. Stopping further production of potentially offending messages is the fastest way to limit continued backlog growth while deeper verification happens.

corrective_actions.action: Inspect the earliest unconsumed offsets on order-events partitions 7 and 2, identify any poison messages, and quarantine, replay, or skip them under incident procedure so those consumers can resume and drain backlog.
corrective_actions.rationale: Impact is isolated to partitions 7 and 2, and the crash-looping pods map directly to those partitions under static assignment. Recovering those specific offsets is the most direct way to restore stuck orders. The runbook for single-consumer lag also points to inspecting the failing offset.

corrective_actions.action: Change orders-worker so bad or forward-incompatible OrderPlaced events do not terminate the process: validate input, handle unknown/optional fields safely, record the offending offset, and route unrecoverable messages to a quarantine path instead of crashing.
corrective_actions.rationale: The confirmed failure mode is repeated process exits on a subset of consumed work. With static assignment and no DLQ, a single bad message can stop an entire partition and strand orders. The worker should fail the message, not the pod.

corrective_actions.action: Add a DLQ/quarantine flow and schema-compatibility controls for OrderPlaced events between checkout-svc and orders-worker, including contract tests in CI/CD for additive field changes.
corrective_actions.rationale: The incident pattern is consistent with consumer fragility to payload variation, and topology confirms there is currently no DLQ. Even if the exact premium-gift-wrap mechanism is later disproven, schema and message-handling guardrails would prevent a single payload change from blocking a partition again.

corrective_actions.action: Add alerts and dashboards for per-partition consumer lag, per-pod restart spikes, and missing worker error telemetry; also ensure crash logs remain searchable during logging maintenance windows.
corrective_actions.rationale: The operational signal that best matched customer impact was partition-specific lag plus pod restarts, while alerts, traces, and logs were inadequate or unavailable. Earlier detection and preserved crash evidence would have shortened triage materially.
